ASSESSMENTS.title: Learner Self-reflection – 24356 (v3)
ASSESSMENTS.subtitle: Apply elementary workshop procedures and processes for a BCATS project

questions.text: Q1: Describe how you would square the end of a board.
questions.hint: Describe the steps: identify face side/edge, mark a 90° line, cut on the waste side, tidy the end, then check squareness.

questions.text: Q2: Describe how you would use a marking gauge to scribe a line parallel to an edge.
questions.hint: Explain: set the distance, lock it, keep the stock against the edge, run the spur along with steady pressure, then store it safely.

questions.text: Q3a: What type of hand saw will you use to cut a steel bar?
questions.hint: Think: fine-toothed frame saw designed for metal.

questions.text: Q3b: What type of hand saw will you use to cut a sheet of MDF?
questions.hint: Think: general timber sheet saw for cutting boards/sheets to size by hand.

questions.text: Q3c: What type of hand saw will you use to cut a 50 x 20mm piece of timber in half (across the grain)?
questions.hint: Across the grain = a saw designed for cross-cutting.

questions.text: Q4: Describe the uses of a smoothing plane.
questions.hint: Cover 2–3 uses: smoothing/finishing surfaces, straightening, and bringing timber down to size.

questions.text: Q5: Plane blades need to be maintained in a sharp condition. How can you protect them from damage when not in use?
questions.hint: Mention cleaning/drying, protecting the edge, and storing the plane safely so the blade can’t hit anything hard.

questions.text: Q6a: What would you use a try square for?
questions.hint: Think: checking and marking 90°/square lines.

questions.text: Q6b: What would you use a combination square for?
questions.hint: Think: marking 90° and 45°; measuring/checking depths and offsets.

questions.text: Q6c: What would you use a steel rule for?
questions.hint: Think: accurate measuring and marking out.

questions.text: Q6d: What would you use a sliding bevel for?
questions.hint: Think: copying/transferring and marking odd angles.

questions.text: Q6e: What would you use a mortise gauge for?
questions.hint: Think: scribing two parallel lines for mortise-and-tenon or dowels.

questions.text: Q7a: What would you use a dovetail saw for?
questions.hint: Think: fine joinery, especially dovetails.

questions.text: Q7b: What would you use a cross cut saw for?
questions.hint: Think: cutting timber to length across the grain.

questions.text: Q7c: What would you use a hack saw for?
questions.hint: Think: cutting metal (and some plastics).

questions.text: Q7d: What would you use a bevelled-edge chisel for?
questions.hint: Think: chopping/paring and cleaning up joints like housings, hinges, dovetails.

questions.text: Q7e: What would you use a jack plane for?
questions.hint: Think: straightening/flattening long timber and general stock removal.

questions.text: Q7f: What would you use a spokeshave for?
questions.hint: Think: smoothing and shaping curves.

questions.text: Q8: Identify the joints you are going to use on your project and the method you have chosen to join the materials together.
questions.hint: Name the joint(s) and how you will assemble them (e.g., glue + clamps, screws, nails, dowels).

questions.text: Q9: What type of finish are you going to use and how are you going to apply it to your project?
questions.hint: State the finish type (e.g., oil/varnish/paint/stain/wax/polyurethane) and how you’ll apply it (prep, coats, method, drying).

ASSESSMENTS.title: Assessment Record Sheet – Workshop processes - Project 1
ASSESSMENTS.subtitle: Record the workshop processes you used for your project

questions.text: Project: What is your project called?
questions.hint: Use the name your teacher uses (e.g., coffee table, toolbox, stool).

questions.text: Materials: What materials were used in this project? (Timber + at least 3 other materials.)
questions.hint: List materials and products, such as timber, plywood/MDF, screws, nails, glue, varnish, polyurethane, paint, metal, plastic, or other materials used.

questions.text: Mark out: What had to be marked out? What tools were used?
questions.hint: Mention measurements and tools (rule/tape, try square, combination square, marking gauge, pencil/knife).

questions.text: Cut/shape: What had to be cut, what had to be shaped, what tools did you use?
questions.hint: Include the parts you cut/shape and the tools (saws, chisels, planes, files, sanders).

questions.text: Joints/jointing: What joints were used in your project? What tools and materials did you need?
questions.hint: Name the joints, and mention tools/materials such as saws, chisels, glue, clamps, drill, pilot holes, screws, nails, dowels, or other fixings.

questions.text: Assemble: What assembling was required? How did you do it?
questions.hint: Explain the order: dry fit, glue, clamp, fixings, check square, clean-up.

questions.text: Finishes: What finishes/finishing were in this project? How did you do them?
questions.hint: Include surface prep, finish type, number of coats, and application method.
